productionBaseline.terminalResourcePolicyCanaryModule: absent in both PH-001 baseline and RED

contractStrengthening.leaseAuthority: RuntimeConfigStore and WsRouter receive one explicit boot-wired authority/validator. Evidence and stable contracts are constructor-time authority inputs; per-call issuance receives only contractId, target, resource, consumer and capability. An identically configured rogue issuer and structural clone are rejected without state mutation.
contractStrengthening.defaultUnavailable: The real registered stable profile set is asserted empty and a default RuntimeConfigStore without an injected authority must return candidate-unavailable. Test-only contracts enter only through the explicit constructor authority seam.
contractStrengthening.rejectionParity: Forged and stale paths compare authoritative consumer configs, target generation/decision/ledger, cleanup registries, queues, connection identities and other-target state before and after rejection.
contractStrengthening.ledgerAccounting: The ledger asserts the exact event delta for selection, capacity+K admissions, rejection, transition and requested/draining/closed rollback, plus the exact retained sequence suffix and dropped count.
contractStrengthening.atomicFailure: The second adapter failure is a valid lease for a missing actual SessionManager session. A fresh first-adapter lease is used, and the actual WS/headless configs plus full target-A canary decision/generation/cleanup/ledger and protected runtime hash must restore exactly to the pre-batch state.
contractStrengthening.callbackBoundary: The fake WebSocket observes rollback state at the post-rollback legacy frame send boundary and requires closed before that frame is sent, proving closure occurs on the final candidate callback.
contractStrengthening.frontendCapability: The frontend matrix includes capability undefined. Its legacy decision has no lease, and passing that absent lease through the scheduler rejection path must preserve queue, stale, snapshot and scheduled state.
